specName: The ADP Plug-in for Visual Studio Code
intent: etalii.adp.ide.vscode produces one installable VS Code extension with the Gartner hype cycle graph and Agent Behavior Modelling diagrams, conforming to their definitions here, with tests, one-step debugging and a pipeline that offers the plug-in for download
context: area: etalii.adp.ide.vscode (plug-in, tests, debug setup, .github/workflows/build.yml, readme, docs/tools.md)
reference: etalii.adp.ide.intellij spec 005-continuous-integration and its naming
reference: etalii.adp.ide.standalone src/diagrams/gartner-hype-cycle-graph and agent-behavior-modelling, pull requests 120 and 122
constraint: constitution principle I, a host implements the definition rather than its own variant
expectations: versioned releases, signing and marketplace publishing
any tool other than the two diagrams
changes to the standalone or IntelliJ hosts
a DISL runtime as a deliverable of its own

decisions.decision: Downloads are the plug-in from each run and a Development build pre-release; versioned releases and marketplaces follow in their own specification
decisions.why: the ask is an artifact to download, and IntelliJ spec 005 is the model

decisions.decision: Markdown stays in the text editor by default; a behavior model is opened by choice, and .ghg opens in the diagram by default
decisions.why: .md is a shared extension in the definition

decisions.decision: Arrange diagram is in scope and both definitions are updated for it in this repository first
decisions.why: standalone has it since pull request 122 and the definitions do not state it yet

decisions.decision: Driving the tools from their .dis files or implementing them by hand is left to the plan (FR-008)
decisions.why: it is a how; FR-006 holds either way

both .dis files hand reading, layout and reordering to plugins and their companions list some forty behaviours DISL 0.1 cannot state; conformance is held by ported standalone tests, vendored fixtures and a test that compares code with the vendored .dis
decisions.rejected: a DISL runtime with plugins; generating code from the .dis
decisions.decision: Both diagram types are implemented by hand in TypeScript against a shared frame; no DISL runtime

decisions.why: the standalone backend owns all diagram logic and an extension that needs nothing installed cannot carry .NET
decisions.rejected: the backend as a child process; .NET as WebAssembly; lifting the 8,000-line React canvas library
decisions.decision: Three layers (core, host, view) with the standalone C# ported function by function and its 274 tests as the checklist

decisions.why: undo, dirty state, save and hot exit are then the platform's, and the text editor and diagram share one history
decisions.rejected: a custom editor with its own document; edits applied in the webview
decisions.decision: Each diagram is a custom text editor over the platform's text document; the view sends intents and the host applies line splices as one WorkspaceEdit

decisions.why: one step of Edit > Undo must restore Markdown and registration together, also for registration-only changes
decisions.rejected: the .adp as a second text document (VS Code asks to undo across files on every undo); writing at once without undo; an undo of the plug-in's own
decisions.decision: A behavior model's registration is held pending, written on save, and tied to the Markdown's undo by an edit log with marker edits

decisions.why: FR-039 prefers a view, a tree view cannot hold inputs, and SVG lets the standalone geometry be copied
decisions.rejected: both inside the editor only; React; Canvas 2D; screenshot comparison
decisions.decision: ADP Toolbox and ADP Properties are webview views in one ADP view container; the canvas is SVG drawn with Preact

decisions.why: the ask is the other implementations' naming and an artifact to download
decisions.rejected: a run-number or -dev version; an OS matrix
decisions.decision: The pipeline takes the IntelliJ workflow's shape: build, real-ide-tests on the packaged .vsix, a development pre-release moved forward with gh, version 0.1.0 unchanged for development builds

decisions.why: FR-060 asks for ratification before the plan is checked, and the frame before the diagram types tests SC-011 by construction
decisions.rejected: one pull request; a plan per repository
decisions.decision: Delivery is one pull request here (definitions with Arrange diagram, re-read at standalone 13b517b3) and six into the VS Code repository, constitution first

concerns.note: Spike S1: a line replaced by itself must be recorded as an undo step and come back with reason undo; if not, FR-031 goes back to clarify before pull request 4
Spike S2: a toolbox drag may not cross from a webview view to the editor's webview; fallback is the toolbox also mounted inside the editor
Open point O1: the definition gives Do the teal fill and Ask the user and Delegate grey, the standalone stylesheet the reverse; the owner rules which side is corrected
setup-plan.ps1 resolved to specs/001-ci-and-badges on develop; the plan was written to specs/006-vscode-plugin by hand, uncommitted in the develop working tree
T024 adds fixtures/registrations/ and T076 adds a member to DiagramType for the heading test; neither is in the plan structure or contracts/frame-api.md yet

plan.summary: TypeScript extension in three layers with hand-built diagram types on a shared frame, custom text editors, an edit log for the registration, IntelliJ-shaped pipeline; 18 decisions, 3 spikes, 6 contracts
plan.risks: S1 marker edit and S2 cross-webview drag rest on undocumented platform behaviour

tasks.summary: 176 tasks in 10 phases across 8 pull requests: 25 setup and foundational (definitions, constitution, skeleton), US1 8, US5 5, US6 7, US4 53, US2 37, US3 30, US7 6, polish 5; tests first in every story; 101 parallel

approach: A TypeScript extension in three layers (pure core, extension host, SVG webviews) where each diagram type is built by hand on a shared frame, porting the standalone C# logic with its tests. Diagrams are custom text editors over the platform's document; the view sends intents and the host applies line splices as one undoable edit, with an edit log tying the .adp registration to the same history. The definitions gain Arrange diagram first, then six pull requests land in the VS Code repository behind an IntelliJ-shaped pipeline.
